title: ModTheSpire2
description:
A pre-launch mod selector and in-game companion manager for Slay the Spire 2.

GitHub:
https://github.com/grassdog0/MTS2

Features:
- Native Windows launcher with no extra runtime install.
- First-pass lightweight Linux and macOS launch scripts for native Steam builds.
- Choose vanilla or selected mods before the game starts.
- Dependency-aware Windows mod list: dependent mods are shown under required mods and cannot be selected until dependencies are selected.
- Compatible with standard mod JSON files, Workshop mod_manifest.json layouts, legacy pck_name manifests, malformed payload-backed manifests, and explicit-id sidecar manifests.
- Custom load order with Move Up, Move Down, numeric order entry, Save Order, Reset Order, and named order profiles on Windows.
- Linux/macOS scripts can launch Vanilla, saved enabled mods, or named profiles from ModTheSpire2Data.
- Saved enabled-mod selections, so a one-time Vanilla launch does not erase your normal mod setup.
- In-game ModTheSpire2 management button on the game's Mod Settings page.
- Clean in-game restart helper: close the current game and reopen the launcher to change enabled mods or profiles.
- Whole-mod changes for DLL/PCK/UI/gameplay/unknown mods are handled through the launcher/restart flow.
- Safe Close and Open Launcher flow to avoid running two game instances at once.
- settings.save backups before ModTheSpire2 writes mod settings.

Important:
Steam Workshop cannot change your Steam launch options automatically.

Windows launch option:
"<path to ModTheSpire2Launcher.exe>" -- %command%

Linux launch option:
"/path/to/ModTheSpire2Launcher.sh" -- %command%

macOS launch option:
"/path/to/ModTheSpire2Launcher.command" -- %command%

Keep %command% exactly as written. Do not replace or remove it. If the game needs extra launch arguments, add them after %command%. Example:

"<path to ModTheSpire2Launcher.exe>" -- %command% --rendering-driver opengl3

Linux/macOS support is currently a lightweight first pass: script menu, native Steam target, no full checkbox GUI yet.

Close and Open Launcher now forwards the current game command line to the launcher, preserving renderer flags such as --rendering-driver opengl3.
changeNote:
Restart argument forwarding fix
- Close and Open Launcher now passes the current game command line to ModTheSpire2Launcher.
- Renderer flags such as --rendering-driver opengl3 are preserved when the launcher reopens the game from the in-game restart flow.
- Windows Steam launch option format remains unchanged: keep %command% exactly as written, and put extra game arguments after %command%.
- Cross-platform lightweight launcher files remain included.
